newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Small Russian Volkhov aluminium sees '97 output up.
newsitem.headline: Small Russian Volkhov aluminium sees '97 output up.

text.p: Russia's small and ageing Volkhov aluminium complex plans to double output of primary aluminium in 1997 to about 20,000 tonnes, a company official said on Friday.
Yevgeny Orlov, the smelter's chief engineer, said the refinery and smelter planned to use capacity idled for economic reasons and to produce about 20,000 tonnes next year.
"Our electricity tariffs are relatively high, but we still want to get production back up to our previous levels," he said from the plant's headquarters near St Petersburg.
Industry sources put Volkhov's total hot metal capacity at anywhere from 25,000 to 60,000 tonnes.

B & D Industrial Group B.V. of Antwerp, which has a 57.6 percent stake in the smelter and is upgrading and replacing some of its old potlines, has said output may rise to 50,000 tonnes a year by the end of 1997.

Interfax news agency said B & D and Vysokoskorostnye Magistraly (High-Speed Railways, or VSM), a Russian concern with a stake in Volkhov, would take a 25-year lease on the Volkhov power plant to try to bring down electricity costs.
It said the refinery and smelter hoped to produce, in addition to aluminium, at least 36,000 tonnes of alumina a year.
VSM will be one of Volkhov's main customers if its multi-billion dollar plan to build a high-speed rail linking Moscow and St Petersburg gets underway.
